rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders told one another to leave the Prophet and persist in worship of their idols.
rows.anchor: وحكى قولهم: أن امشوا واصبروا على آلهتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He takes the means as routes or gates of heaven and cites an anonymous poetic line using أسباب السماء.
rows.anchor: وأبواب السماء: أسبابها، قال الشاعر :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the means are ropes by which one climbs to heaven, as the unbelievers had asked the Prophet to ascend and bring them a book.
rows.anchor: ويكون أيضا فليرتقوا في الأسباب، أي: في الحبال إلى السماء، كما سألوك أن ترقى في السماء وتأتيهم بكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To rise through the means is also an Arabic idiom for excelling in knowledge or another field, like reaching heaven.
rows.anchor: ويقال للرجل إذا تقدم في العلم وغيره وبرع: قد ارتقى في الأسباب، كما يقال: قد بلغ السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He compares the challenge to the question whether the unbelievers have a ladder for a listener to ascend and bring clear authority.
rows.anchor: ونحو هذا قوله في موضع آخر: أم لهم سلم يستمعون فيه فليأت مستمعهم بسلطان مبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questions about mercy's treasuries and the heavens' dominion reproach the idolaters and establish their incapacity.
rows.anchor: أعندهم بآلهتهم هذه خزائن الرحمة؟! أم لهم ملك السماوات والأرض وما بينهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جند means a faction or party gathered around the idols.
rows.anchor: وجند بمعنى: حزب لهذه الآلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما in جند ما is an extra particle.
rows.anchor: وجند بمعنى: حزب لهذه الآلهة. و (ما) زائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مهزوم means subdued and humiliated; its root sense is breaking, as in a broken depression, a broken army, or a ruptured waterskin.
rows.anchor: ومهزوم: مقموع ذليل. وأصل الهزم: الكسر، ومنه قيل للنفرة في الأرض: هزمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idol faction is humbled by these trials and claims because it can establish none of these powers for its gods or itself.
rows.anchor: هم حزب عند ذلك مقموع ذليل من الأحزاب، أي عند هذه المحن، وعند هذا القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The الأحزاب are earlier disbelievers, named for banding together against their prophets.
rows.anchor: والأحزاب: سائر من تقدمهم من الكفار، سموا أحزابا لأنهم تحزبوا على أنبيائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following list of earlier peoples and the phrase أولئك الأحزاب identify Quraysh's polytheists as one of those factions.
rows.anchor: فأعلمنا أن مشركي قريش حزب من هؤلاء الأحزاب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, in the report of Abu Salih, understood the passage to tell the Prophet that the polytheists would be defeated at Badr.
rows.anchor: وكان ابن عباس في رواية أبي صالح- يذهب إلى أن الله تعالى أخبر رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه سيهزم المشركين يوم بدر

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: One interpretation says God appointed Adam over his descendants and entrusted him with authority over animals, commands, prohibitions, and permitted matters; Adam accepted and carried the trust.
rows.anchor: إن الله، جل ذكره، لما استخلف آدم على ذريته، وسلطه على جميع ما في الأرض من الأنعام والطير والوحش

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: In this account, Adam was ordered to present the trust to the heavens under a condition of reward for obedience and punishment for disobedience; they refused from fear.
rows.anchor: فأمره أن يعرض ذلك على السموات بالشرط الذي أخذ عليه من الثواب إن أطاع، ومن العقاب إن عصى

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: The earth and mountains also refused, while Adam's descendants accepted the trust without the fear shown by heaven, earth, and mountains, ignorant of its consequences.
rows.anchor: ثم أمره أن يعرض ذلك على الأرض والجبال، فكلها أباه. ثم أمره أن يعرضه على ولده، فعرضه عليه فقبله بالشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, carrying the trust exposes the hypocrites' hypocrisy and the polytheists' idolatry for punishment, while the believers' faith appears and God accepts their repentance.
rows.anchor: فإذا تقلده ظهر نفاق المنافق وشرك المشرك، فعذبه الله به، وظهر إيمان المؤمن فتاب الله عليه

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: An alternative interpretation identifies the trust as the religious obligations, presented with their rewards and punishments; the heavens, earth, and mountains declined, but humanity accepted.
rows.anchor: وفيه قول آخر: قالوا: الأمانة: الفرائض، عرضت على السموات والأرض والجبال بما فيها من الثواب والعقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the two interpretations are close in meaning.
rows.anchor: والمعنيان في التفسيرين متقاربان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa on ḍād, الضر is the opposite of benefit; it can mean inability to bring gain or avert harm.
rows.anchor: الضر: بفتح الضاد- ضد النفع، قال الله عز وجل: هل يسمعونكم إذ تدعون أو ينفعونكم أو يضرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الضر can also mean hardship or affliction.
rows.anchor: والضر: الشدة والبلاء، كقوله: وإن يمسسك الله بضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One form of hardship is drought: the mercy after hardship in the cited verse means rain after drought and barrenness.
rows.anchor: فمن الشدة: قحط المطر، قال الله تعالى: وإذا أذقنا الناس رحمة من بعد ضراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الضر can denote the terror of danger at sea.
rows.anchor: ومنه: الهول، كقوله: وإذا مسكم الضر في البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word can mean illness, as in Job's complaint and the verse about a person in distress calling on God.
rows.anchor: ومنه المرض، كقول أيوب عليه السلام: أني مسني الضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الضر can also mean loss or diminution, as in the statement that disbelievers will not harm God at all.
rows.anchor: ومنه النقص، كقوله تعالى: لن يضروا الله شيئا وسيحبط أعمالهم

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: The objectors report that Uthman saw a grammatical error in the codex and said the Arabs would correct it with their tongues.
rows.anchor: ورويتم عن عثمان أنه نظر في المصحف فقال: أرى فيه لحنا وستقيمه العرب بألسنتها

words: لَّا يُسْـَٔلُ عَن ذَنۢبِهِۦٓ إِنسٌۭ وَلَا جَآنٌّۭ
rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: The objectors allege a contradiction between saying no human or jinn is asked about sin and saying God will question everyone about their deeds.
rows.anchor: وقالوا: وهل التناقض إلا مثل قوله: فيومئذ لا يسئل عن ذنبه إنس ولا جان

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: They contrast the claim that people will not speak or be allowed to excuse themselves with verses describing disputes before God and a demand for proof.
rows.anchor: ومثل قوله: هذا يوم لا ينطقون

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: They allege inconsistency between the afterlife scene of people questioning one another and the statement that there will be no kinship or mutual questioning.
rows.anchor: ومثل قوله: وأقبل بعضهم على بعض يتساءلون

words: ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَهِىَ دُخَانٌۭ
rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: They argue that Fussilat places the earth's creation before the heavens, whereas al-Naziat appears to place the heaven's construction before the earth's spreading.
rows.anchor: وقال بعد ذلك: ثم استوى إلى السماء وهي دخان فقال لها وللأرض ائتيا طوعا أو كرها

words: ليس لهم طعام إلا من ضريع
rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: They ask how hell can contain the thorn plant if fire consumes plants and another verse says its only food is ghislin.
rows.anchor: ومثل قوله: ليس لهم طعام إلا من ضريع

words: وما كان الله ليعذبهم وأنت فيهم
rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: They contrast the promise not to punish while the Prophet is among them or they seek forgiveness with the question why God should not punish those who bar the Sacred Mosque.
rows.anchor: وما كان الله ليعذبهم وأنت فيهم

words: فانكحوا ما طاب لكم من النساء مثنى وثلاث ورباع
rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: They question how the command to marry women relates to the condition about acting justly toward orphan girls.
rows.anchor: وقالوا: فأين قوله: وإن خفتم ألا تقسطوا في اليتامى، من قوله: فانكحوا ما طاب لكم من النساء مثنى وثلاث ورباع

words: انطلقوا إلى ما كنتم به تكذبون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day the sun nears people's heads, they lack clothing or shelter, and its heat and the day's distress overwhelm them; God mercifully saves whom He wills to shade.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن الشمس تدنو من رؤوس الخلائق، وليس عليهم يومئذ لباس، ولا لهم كنان، فتلفحهم الشمس وتسفعهم وتأخذ بأنفاسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers are sent from that distress to shade made of the smoke of Hell, which divides into three branches as great smoke rises.
rows.anchor: انطلقوا من ذلك إلى ظل من دخان نار جهنم قد سطع ثم افترق ثلاث فرق، وكذلك شأن الدخان العظيم إذا ارتفع أن يتشعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They remain in this smoke until judgment ends, as God's friends remain under the Throne's shade or another shade, after which each group is sent to its final abode.
rows.anchor: فيكونون فيه إلى أن يفرغ من الحساب، كما يكون أولياء الله في ظل عرشه أو حيث شاء من الظل

words: لَّا ظَلِيلٍۢ وَلَا يُغْنِى مِنَ ٱللَّهَبِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This shade does not protect them from the day's heat; it brings them closer to a flame hotter than the sun and offers no protection from it.
rows.anchor: لا يظلكم من حر هذا اليوم بل يدنيكم من لهب النار إلى ما هو أشد عليكم من حر الشمس

words: لَّا ظَلِيلٍۢ وَلَا يُغْنِى مِنَ ٱللَّهَبِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He compares this to the shade of yahmum, which commentators identify as smoke and as the canopy of Hell's inhabitants; it is neither cool nor gracious.
rows.anchor: وهذا مثل قوله سبحانه: وظل من يحموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers who give ṣād sukūn in القصر compare the sparks to a palace or structure among the desert Arabs' water installations.
rows.anchor: فمن قرأه بتسكين الصاد، أراد القصر من قصور مياه الأعراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readers compare the sparks to palm trunks or their bases when cut.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأه القصر شبهه بأعناق النخل، ويقال: بأصوله إذا قطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sparks are like palaces in their size and like yellow camels in color; Arabs call black camels yellow because black coats contain a tinge of yellow.
rows.anchor: ووقع تشبيه الشرر بالقصر في مقاديره، ثم شبهه في لونه بالجمالات الصفر وهي السود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The anonymous poetic line uses صفر for black camels, supporting the gloss of the verse's yellow camels; he also notes that white gazelles are called أدم because their whiteness is clouded.
rows.anchor: هن صفر أولادها كالزبيب أي: هن سود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic uses enduring conditions such as night and day differing, the sea rising, a mountain standing, or heaven and earth enduring to mean forever.
rows.anchor: فإن للعرب في معنى (الأبد) ألفاظا يستعملونها في كلامهم، يقولون: لا أفعل ذلك ما اختلف الليل والنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He first interprets the duration as the lifetime of the world, since heaven and earth will change at the end; the exception allows added duration beyond that term.
rows.anchor: وللسماء وللأرض وقت يتغيران فيه عن هيئتهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غير مجذوذ means uncut off or uninterrupted.
rows.anchor: ثم قال: عطاء غير مجذوذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here إلا means سوى, as in the idiom of staying a year in a house except for whatever one wills to add to the year.
rows.anchor: و (إلا) في هذا الموضع بمعنى (سوى) ومثله من الكلام: لأسكنن في هذه الدار حولا إلا ما شئت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes the expression as the Arabs' conventional word for eternity and the exception as the people's time on earth before they entered Paradise or Hell.
rows.anchor: وفيه (قول آخر) ، وهو: أن يجعل دوام السماء والأرض بمعنى الأبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation makes the exception the sinful Muslims' time in Hell until God's mercy and the Prophet's intercession remove them to Paradise; the garden's exception likewise covers their prior stay in Hell.
rows.anchor: وفيه (وجه ثالث) : وهو أن يكون الاستثناء من الخلود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the Torah's statement that God rested on the seventh day through ordinary usage: rest first follows exhausting effort, then shifts to finishing a task, and finally to turning one's attention toward something.
rows.anchor: وأصل الاستراحة: أن تكون في معاناة شيء ينصبك ويتعبك، فتستريح. ثم ينتقل ذلك فتصير الاستراحة بمعنى: الفراغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God is never occupied by one matter over another, سنفرغ لكم means He will turn to address the two groups after a long period of leaving them unhurried.
rows.anchor: والله تبارك وتعالى لا يشغله شأن عن شأن. ومجازه: سنقصد لكم بعد طول الترك والإمهال

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says God's attention to creation is near, meaning the Hour has drawn close and its signs have appeared.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: قد دنا من الله فراغ لخلقه. يريد: أن الساعة قد أزفت وجاء أشراطها

words: فِىٓ أَىِّ صُورَةٍۢ مَّا شَآءَ رَكَّبَكَ
rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some read the verse as transmigration of souls, but Ibn Qutayba rejects that reading and says the address is not to one particular person.
rows.anchor: وتأول قوم في قوله تعالى: في أي صورة ما شاء ركبك

words: فِىٓ أَىِّ صُورَةٍۢ مَّا شَآءَ رَكَّبَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is generic, as in O human, striving toward your Lord; God formed and proportioned people in whatever forms He chose, in beauty, ugliness, whiteness, blackness, dark complexion, or redness.
rows.anchor: كما يقول القائل: يا أيها الرجل، وكلكم ذلك الرجل

words: فِىٓ أَىِّ صُورَةٍۢ مَّا شَآءَ رَكَّبَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links the variety of chosen human forms and colors to the signs in the creation of the heavens and earth and the variation of human languages and colors.
rows.anchor: ونحوه قوله: ومن آياته خلق السماوات والأرض واختلاف ألسنتكم وألوانكم

words: فِىٓ أَىِّ صُورَةٍۢ مَّا شَآءَ رَكَّبَكَ
rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say God's utterance is not real speech but the production of meanings, and treat much Quranic speech metaphorically, like saying a wall spoke when it leaned.
rows.anchor: وذهب قوم في قول الله وكلامه: إلى أنه ليس قولا ولا كلاما على الحقيقة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret God's command that the angels prostrate to Adam as inspiration, comparing it to God's inspiration of the bee and interpreting revelation in another verse as inspiration.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم في قوله للملائكة: اسجدوا لآدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He allows that القول can be called revelation, as can gestures and lip or eyebrow signals; any sign that conveys meaning may be called revelation, while the bee's revelation is its being directed to build, follow paths, and eat fruit.
rows.anchor: فما ننكر أن القول قد يسمى وحيا، والإيماء وحيا، والرمز بالشفتين والحاجبين وحيا، والإلهام وحيا

rows.speaker: العجاج
rows.claim: Al-Ajjaj's verse about the earth uses وحي for making it settle, illustrating revelation as subjection or directing.
rows.anchor: وحي لها القرار فاستقرت أي: سخرها لأن تستقر

words: إِلَّا وَحْيًا أَوْ مِن وَرَآءِ حِجَابٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He distinguishes three forms: God shows prophets visions in sleep, speaks to Moses from behind a veil, and sends the faithful spirit as a messenger to whom He wills.
rows.anchor: فالوحي الأول: ما أراه الله تعالى الأنبياء في منامهم. والكلام من وراء الحجاب: تكليمه موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person who is only inspired is not said to have been spoken to by God; Ibn Qutayba insists on a distinction between speech and saying.
rows.anchor: ولا يقال لمن ألهمه الله: كلمه الله، لما أعلمتك من الفرق بين (الكلام) (والقول)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects reducing God's prolonged exchanges with the angels and Iblis about prostration, expulsion, and reprieve to inspiration; that would make no sense, especially if inspiration compels obedience.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون قوله للملائكة وإبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects interpreting the address to heaven and earth as mere creation or Hell's speech as a report of capacity, asking why strained evasions are needed when scripture allows creatures to speak.
rows.anchor: وأما تأويلهم في قوله جل وعز للسماء والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can make skins, hands, and feet speak, and can make mountains and birds praise; this supports taking the speech of heaven and earth as possible.
rows.anchor: وما في نطق جهنم ونطق السماء والأرض من العجب؟ والله تبارك وتعالى ينطق الجلود، والأيدي، والأرجل

words: قُلْ أُوحِىَ إِلَىَّ أَنَّهُ ٱسْتَمَعَ نَفَرٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلْجِنِّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is difficult because إن recurs with differences between accusative and genitive readings and uncertainty over whether statements belong to God or the jinn, so he explains the whole surah.
rows.anchor: في هذه السورة إشكال وغموض: بما وقع فيها من تكرار (إن) واختلاف القراء في نصبها وكسرها

words: قُلْ أُوحِىَ إِلَىَّ أَنَّهُ ٱسْتَمَعَ نَفَرٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلْجِنِّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn listened to the Prophet reciting Quran and, when they returned to their people, told them they had heard a wondrous Quran.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى لنبيه: قل أوحي إلي أنه استمع نفر من الجن وكانوا استمعوا لرسول الله، صلى الله عليه وسلم، وهو يقرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جد ربنا means that our Lord is exalted or great; the idiom jad fulan fi qawmihi means that he became esteemed among his people.
rows.anchor: ثم قال: وأنه تعالى جد ربنا ما اتخذ صاحبة ولا ولدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn call their foolish or ignorant member's speech about God an excess of lying and injustice.
rows.anchor: وأنه كان يقول سفيهنا على الله شططا

words: أَن لَّن تَقُولَ ٱلْإِنسُ وَٱلْجِنُّ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn say they had previously trusted people, assuming no one would lie about God; their speech ends here.
rows.anchor: يقولون: كنا نتوهم أن أحدا لا يقول على الله باطلا. يريدون: إنا كنا قبل اليوم نصدقهم ونحن نظن أن أحدا لا يكذب على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says إن is genitive in all these clauses except أنه استمع.
rows.anchor: وانقطع هاهنا قول الجن. و (إن) في جميع هذا مكسورة إلا (أنه استمع)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In verse 6, وأنه may be accusative and coordinated with the earlier revelation clause, or genitive as a new statement from God.
rows.anchor: فإن شئت أن تنصب وأنه وتردها إلى قوله: قل أوحي إلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In pre-Islamic travel, a man who reached a desolate place would seek refuge in its chief from the jinn's foolish members.
rows.anchor: وكان الرجل في الجاهلية إذا سافر فصار إلى موضع مقفر موحش لا أنيس به، قال: أعوذ بسيد هذا المكان من سفهائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking the jinn's protection increases their arrogance and sin, leading them to claim mastery over both jinn and humans.
rows.anchor: يريد أنهم يزدادون بهذا التعوذ طغيانا وإثما فيقولون: سدنا الجن والإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn, like the humans addressed, thought that God would not resurrect anyone and thus did not believe in resurrection.
rows.anchor: يقول: ظن الجن كما ظننتم أيها الإنس أن لا بعث يوم القيامة. أي كانوا لا يؤمنون بالبعث كما أنكم لا تؤمنون به

words: وَجَآءَتْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍۢ مَّعَهَا سَآئِقٌۭ وَشَهِيدٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The driver is the person's devil companion, called a driver because he follows even without urging or pushing; the Prophet was said to drive his companions by walking behind them.
rows.anchor: السائق هاهنا: قرينها من الشياطين، سمي سائقا، لأنه يتبعها وإن لم يحثها ويدفعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The witness is the angel who testifies to the person's deeds.
rows.anchor: والشهيد: الملك الشاهد عليها بما عملت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person had been heedless of this in worldly life; God removes the cover by showing what had been hidden from him.
rows.anchor: يقول الله تعالى: لقد كنت في غفلة من هذا في الدنيا. فكشفنا عنك غطاءك أي: أريناك ما كان مستورا عنك في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the cover is removed, the person's sight is piercing.
rows.anchor: فبصرك اليوم حديد أي: فأنت ثاقب البصر لما كشف عنك الغطاء

words: وَقَالَ قَرِينُهُۥ هَٰذَا مَا لَدَىَّ عَتِيدٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here قرينه is the angel, who says the person's recorded deeds are present with him.
rows.anchor: وقال قرينه يعني: الملك. هذا ما لدي عتيد يعني: ما كتبه من عمله، حاضر عندي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to cast the denier into Hell is attributed by some to the angel and by others to God.
rows.anchor: ألقيا في جهنم كل كفار عنيد يقال: هو قول الملك، ويقال: قول الله جل ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion who denies making the man transgress is his devil from among the jinn.
rows.anchor: وقال قرينه من الشياطين: ربنا ما أطغيته ولكن كان في ضلال بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links the pairing of wrongdoers with their companions to Arab usage of pairing one camel with another and to the verse about pairing people with fair companions.
rows.anchor: وهذا مثل قوله سبحانه: احشروا الذين ظلموا وأزواجهم

words: فَحَقَّ عَلَيْنَا قَوْلُ رَبِّنَآ إِنَّا لَذَآئِقُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dialogue means that both the human and his companion will taste punishment.
rows.anchor: يعني: نحن وأنتم ذائقون العذاب، وقد تقدم تفسير هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command not to dispute before God addresses the criminals and their devil companions.
rows.anchor: يعني: المجرمين وقرناءهم من الشياطين وقد قدمت إليكم بالوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's word cannot be shifted, distorted, increased, or diminished, because He knows how the people strayed and how their companions led them astray.
rows.anchor: أي: لا يغير عن جهته، ولا يحرف، ولا يزاد فيه ولا ينقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People reluctant to attribute sins to prophets resort to forced readings that conflict with scripture, though the wording and meaning do not support those evasions.
rows.anchor: يستوحش كثير من الناس من أن يلحقوا بالأنبياء ذنوبا، ويحملهم التنزيه لهم، صلوات الله عليهم، على مخالفة كتاب الله جل ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some explain Adam's غوى as indigestion from eating the tree, relying on an Arab expression for a calf that drank too much milk; Ibn Qutayba rejects the strained gloss as lexically unsound.
rows.anchor: كتأولهم في قوله تعالى: وعصى آدم ربه فغوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited idiom for becoming overfull has a different vocalization from غوى in Adam's verse; here misguidance matches disobedience, the opposite of guidance just as disobedience opposes obedience.
rows.anchor: وذلك غوى- بفتح الواو- يغوي غيا. وهو من البشم غوي- بكسر الواو- يغوى غوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's line about a bow uses the word غوى in the sense of dying from overfeeding, to illustrate the proposed idiom.
rows.anchor: معطفة الأثناء ليس فصيلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam ate the forbidden tree after Satan deceived him with a false oath of sincere advice; this was not a premeditated act from settled hostility like the sins of God's enemies.
rows.anchor: وقد أكل آدم، صلى الله عليه وسلم، من الشجرة التي نهي عنها باستزلال إبليس وخدائعه إياه بالله والقسم به إنه لمن الناصحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's verbs عصى and غوى describe Adam's act, but he should not be labeled inherently disobedient or astray because the act did not arise from prior intent or become a repeated trait.
rows.anchor: كما قال الله تعالى، ولا نقول: آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He compares describing a one-time act without assigning a lasting label to saying someone cut and sewed a garment without calling him a tailor until the work is habitual.
rows.anchor: كما تقول لرجل قطع ثوبا وخاطه: قد قطعه وخاطه، ولا تقل خائط ولا خياط حتى يكون معاودا لذلك الفعل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say Joseph intended to commit the sin while the woman intended it; Ibn Qutayba rejects that reading in light of the stated sign from his Lord.
rows.anchor: وكتأولهم في قوله سبحانه: ولقد همت به وهم بها أنها همت بالمعصية

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another reported explanation says Joseph intended to strike her, which Ibn Qutayba also challenges.
rows.anchor: وقال (بعضهم) : وهم بضربها! والله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He asks whether Joseph could have intended escape or a blow and then, upon seeing the divine sign, remained; this challenges those proposed explanations.
rows.anchor: أفتراه أراد الفرار منها. أو الضرب لها، فلما رأى البرهان أقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Persia had defeated the Romans in the Jazira, the nearest Roman land to Persian rule; Quraysh rejoiced, while Muslims favored the scriptural Romans over the Zoroastrian Persians.
rows.anchor: كانت (فارس) غلبت (الروم) على أرض الجزيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Romans are the subject who will defeat Persia after their own defeat; غلبهم can refer either to victors' victory or the defeated party's loss.
rows.anchor: وهم من بعد غلبهم أي: والروم من بعد أن غلبوا سيغلبون أهل فارس. وغلبهم يكون للغالبين والمغلوبين جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بضع means more than three and fewer than ten years; the Romans defeated Persia and drove them from their territory on the day of Hudaybiya.
rows.anchor: في بضع سنين والبضع: ما فوق الثلاث ودون العشر. فغلبت الروم أهل فارس وأخرجوهم من بلادهم يوم الحديبية

words: لِلَّهِ ٱلْأَمْرُ مِن قَبْلُ وَمِنۢ بَعْدُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God controls victory before and after and grants it to whomever He wills.
rows.anchor: لله الأمر من قبل ومن بعد أي: له الغلبة لمن شاء من قبل ومن بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers rejoice when the People of the Book defeat the Magians.
rows.anchor: ويومئذ أي: يوم يغلب الروم أهل فارس يفرح المؤمنون بنصر الله أهل الكتاب على المجوس

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi says the Conquest surah came after Hudaybiya; the believers were pardoned, pledged the pledge of approval, received Khaybar's dates, and rejoiced when Roman victory confirmed God's scripture.
rows.anchor: قال الشعبي في سورة الفتح: أنزلت بعد الحديبية، فغفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه وما تأخر، وبايعوه مبايعة الرضوان
